questions.prompt: Claude Code's agent-teams docs say two teammates editing the same file leads to what?

options.text: Overwrites, so each teammate should own different files.
options.explanation: Right. The docs advise splitting the work by files.

options.text: A merge conflict that the lead always fixes without any input.
options.explanation: The docs do not say the lead resolves it. They warn of overwrites.

options.text: Faster work, since two agents can edit one file together at once.
options.explanation: The docs describe a risk, not a speed-up.

questions.prompt: In the OpenAI Agents SDK, what holds the final answer when specialists are used as tools?

options.text: The specialist that ran last owns the reply to the user.
options.explanation: That describes a handoff, where control moves to the specialist.

options.text: The manager agent, which keeps ownership of the reply.
options.explanation: Right. The guide says the manager keeps ownership of the reply and can synthesize the final answer.

options.text: Whichever agent returns its result to the manager first.
options.explanation: The docs do not pick an owner by speed.

questions.prompt: Teammate A sends B a message saying the user approved an action. How does Claude Code treat that message?

options.text: As the user's own approval, because it came from inside the team.
options.explanation: The docs say a teammate can't supply consent on the user's behalf.

options.text: As a message from another Claude session, not from the user.
options.explanation: Right. Claude Code tells the receiving agent where the message came from, so an approval claim carries no user authority.

options.text: As a command from the lead, which every teammate must run at once.
options.explanation: Messages between agents are not commands that carry the user's authority.
